name: Coprime Arrays
description: Let's call an array a of size n coprime iff gcd ( a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ) = 1 , where gcd is the greatest common divisor of the arguments. You are given two numbers n and k . For each i ( 1 ≤ i ≤ k ) you have to determine the number of coprime arrays a of size n such that for every j ( 1 ≤ j ≤ n ) 1 ≤ a j ≤ i . Since the answers can be very large, you have to calculate them modulo 10 9 + 7 .
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and k ( 1 ≤ n , k ≤ 2·10 6 ) — the size of the desired arrays and the maximum upper bound on elements, respectively.
output_specification: Since printing 2·10 6 numbers may take a lot of time, you have to output the answer in such a way: Let b i be the number of coprime arrays with elements in range [1, i ] , taken modulo 10 9 + 7 . You have to print , taken modulo 10 9 + 7 . Here denotes bitwise xor operation ( ^ in C++ or Java, xor in Pascal).
approach_summary: Apply Euclidean Algorithm paradigm under the Number Theory framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
